subject.title: Cross-provider fallback should respect provider trust boundaries for images/attachments

question: Should OpenClaw treat configured cross-provider model fallback as consent to transfer user media, or add a separate provider media trust policy for fallback retries?
rationale: The source shows a real privacy boundary gap, but the permanent default affects compatibility, fallback usefulness, and sensitive-data disclosure, which requires maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Add explicit media trust policy
options.body: Add a config/docs/runtime policy that preserves current behavior by default but lets users restrict images and attachments on cross-provider fallback.

options.title: Document fallback as full consent
options.body: Keep current forwarding semantics and document that configured cross-provider fallbacks may receive prompt text and media.

options.title: Fail closed for cross-provider media
options.body: Strip cross-provider media by default and require users to opt back into forwarding when they want fallback vision behavior.

recommendation.title: Add explicit media trust policy
recommendation.body: Add a config/docs/runtime policy that preserves current behavior by default but lets users restrict images and attachments on cross-provider fallback.
